title: West African Drumming
objective: After this level you can describe West African drumming and the role of griots.
summary: Yoruba dundun drums 'talk' by changing pitch to follow a tonal language; in Ewe Agbadza a repeating bell time line aligns the drums; griots (jeli) carry history in song, often with the 21-string kora.

cards.headline: In Yoruba music, a drum can recite poetry.
cards.body: Among the Yoruba of Nigeria, dundun drums are used as talking drums, accompanying oriki, praise-name poetry. Talking drums imitate the rhythm and the rise and fall of spoken words. In this level, West African music does three jobs at once: drums that speak, a bell that holds an ensemble together, and musicians who carry history.

cards.headline: How a drum talks
cards.body: The dundun is an hourglass-shaped pressure drum. Cords run between its two heads, and the drummer holds it under one arm. Squeeze the cords and the head tightens, changing the pitch. That matters because Yoruba is a tonal language: the pitch of a syllable can change a word's meaning. So a drum that slides between pitches can follow the melody of speech, and skilled drummers reproduce proverbs and praise songs.

cards.headline: Agbadza: the bell keeps everyone together
cards.body: Among the Ewe of Ghana and Togo, Agbadza is widely seen as the Ewe music and dance. Its drummers play in layers: a low lead sogo drum and a response kidi drum trade phrases over a kagan drum, an axatse rattle, handclaps and the gankogui bell. The bell repeats one phrase, 2+2+1+2+2+2+1, a time line heard across West Africa. That phrase is everyone's reference point, keeping every layer of the polyrhythm lined up.

mascot.line: Lose your place? Listen for the bell. It never wanders.

cards.headline: Griots: musicians who carry history
cards.body: Griots, called jeli or jali in Mande languages, are hereditary West African troubadour-historians. They preserve genealogies, historical narratives and oral traditions, sing praise songs, and have served as advisers and diplomats. Many play the kora, a long-necked harp-lute with 21 strings and a calabash gourd resonator, played with four fingers. In a griot's hands, one song can be a history lesson, a family tree and a tribute at once.

questions.prompt: Who are griots, or jeli, in West African tradition?

options.label: Craftsmen who carve and tune the talking drums
options.rationale: Griots are musicians and historians, not instrument makers.

options.label: Priests who lead the ceremonies of the royal court
options.rationale: Gamelan comes from Java and Bali.

options.label: Dancers who perform only at weddings and funerals
options.rationale: Griots sing history and praise, and have served as advisers.

questions.explanation: Griots are hereditary troubadour-historians who keep genealogies, histories and oral traditions alive, often playing the kora.

questions.prompt: Why can a squeezed dundun drum 'talk' in Yoruba?

options.label: It taps out the letters of each word in a code
options.rationale: It follows the pitch and rhythm of speech, not an alphabet.

options.label: It plays one fixed pitch fast enough to sound like speech
options.rationale: A fixed pitch couldn't follow the tones of words.

options.label: Yoruba is tonal, and squeezing the cords changes the drum's pitch
Its sound carries farther than a human voice

questions.explanation: Yoruba is a tonal language, so a drum whose pitch rises and falls can imitate its words.

questions.prompt: Level 51 said much African music layers contrasting rhythms at once. In Ewe Agbadza, what keeps those layers aligned?

options.label: A conductor with a baton
options.rationale: No conductor is needed; the bell is the reference.

options.label: A written score each drummer reads
options.rationale: The reference is a sound everyone hears.

options.label: Every drummer playing the same rhythm
options.rationale: The layers are different on purpose.

options.label: The gankogui bell's repeating time line

questions.explanation: The bell repeats a 2+2+1+2+2+2+1 phrase that keeps every part in polyrhythmic alignment.
